name: Amazon Bedrock
description: Observe end-to-end generative AI models provided by Amazon Bedrock.
details:
## Overview

Amazon Bedrock provides an easy way to build and scale generative AI applications with foundation models. 

Bedrock is an end-to-end managed service that offers a choice of high-performing foundation models from leading AI companies like AI21 Labs, Anthropic, Cohere, Luma, Meta, Mistral AI, poolside, Stability AI, and Amazon through a single API. It also provides the broad set of capabilities you need to build generative AI applications with security, privacy, and responsible AI. 

Dynatrace provides a solution for tracking and revealing the full context of used technologies and service interaction topology, analyzing security vulnerabilities, and observing metrics, traces, logs, and business events in real time—all done automatically and safely.

## Use cases

### Monitor service health and performance
- Detect bottlenecks by tracking real-time metrics, including request counts, durations, and error rates.
- Manage service costs with automated cost calculations for each request. 
- Stay on track with SLOs.

### Monitor guardrails to ensure compliance 
- Monitor your safeguards customized to your application requirements and responsible AI policies.
- Validate toxicity, filtered content, and denied topics to ensure compliance. 
- Prevent PII leaks. 
- Prevent quality degradation by validating models and usage patterns in real time.

### End-to-end tracing and debugging
- Achieve complete visibility of prompt flows, from initial request to final response, for faster root cause analysis.
- Capture detailed debug data to troubleshoot issues in complex pipelines.
- Streamline your workflows with granular tracing of LLM prompts, including response latency and model-level metrics.
- Resolve issues quicker by pinpointing exact problem areas in prompts, tokens, or system integrations.

details:

By instrumenting your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Dynatrace, you get continuous visibility into agent behavior, tool usage, dependencies, guardrails, and model interactions across your whole stack.

## Get started

Set up end-to-end observability for your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents with Dynatrace OneAgent and OpenTelemetry, then analyze them in the [AI Observability app](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/shortlink/app-ai-observability) (Hub app ID `dynatrace.genai.observability`).

Pick the example that matches your setup:
- **You deploy your own agent into AgentCore Runtime:** OneAgent auto-instruments the agent's Bedrock calls from the inside. See [aws-bedrock-agents/oneagent on GitHub](https://github.com/dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-ai-agent-instrumentation-examples/tree/main/aws-bedrock-agents/oneagent).
- **You call a fully managed AgentCore harness (`invoke_harness`):** wrap the call in an OpenTelemetry span with `gen_ai.*` attributes. This needs OneAgent on the host with the **OpenTelemetry (Python) [Opt-In]** OneAgent feature enabled. See [aws-bedrock-agentcore/oneagent-opentelemetry on GitHub](https://github.com/dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-ai-agent-instrumentation-examples/tree/main/aws-bedrock-agentcore/oneagent-opentelemetry).

name: Arize AX
description: Analyze traces, latency, and evals of LLM apps through Arize OpenInference data.
details:
## Overview

Arize AX, from Arize, a Dynatrace company, is the AI engineering platform for improving AI agents and applications. It gives AI engineers one workflow to capture what their agents actually do, find where they fail, measure quality, and prove every change before it ships.

Arize AX captures traces of real agent behavior, including inputs, outputs, tool calls, and costs. Signal automatically groups recurring failures into ranked issues with trace evidence and a proposed fix. Evaluators score quality continuously against criteria you define, and experiments turn every prompt, model, or retrieval change into a controlled comparison.

Alyx, the AI engineering agent built into Arize AX, works across every step. Ask it in plain language which tool calls are failing, which requests your agent can't handle, or how to build an evaluator.

This is intended for teams who:
- Build AI agents or LLM applications and need to understand why they fail in production.
- Want to move from ad hoc prompt tweaks to measurable, repeatable improvement.

## Get started

**Instrument with OpenInference.** Arize AX tracing is built on OpenInference, the open, OpenTelemetry-based standard for AI tracing created by Arize, with pre-built auto-instrumentation for 30+ providers and frameworks.

### Get started for free in one command
Run `npx evals` from your terminal. It launches your coding agent, signs you up for a free Arize AX account, and instruments your app. Python users can run `uvx arize-ax-cli instrument` instead.

### Or set up step by step
1. [Sign up](https://app.arize.com/auth/join) for a free Arize AX account.
2. Instrument your agent with [auto-instrumentation](https://arize.com/docs/ax/instrument/set-up-tracing) to capture your first trace.
3. [Enable Signal](https://arize.com/docs/ax/get-started/get-started-managed-agent) on your project and review your first issue.
4. [Create evaluators](https://arize.com/docs/ax/get-started/get-started-evaluations) and [run experiments](https://arize.com/docs/ax/get-started/get-started-improve-your-agent) to prove a fix.

Using Claude, Cursor, or Codex? See [coding agent setup](https://arize.com/docs/ax/set-up-with-ai-assistants).

## Use cases

### Find where your agents fail
- Capture every agent run as a trace, including inputs, outputs, tool calls, and costs.
- Enable Signal to group recurring failures into ranked issues, each with trace evidence and a proposed fix.
- Ask Alyx in plain language to find failing runs, and add dashboards and alerts for ongoing visibility.

### Score quality against your own criteria
- Evaluate agent performance with LLM-as-a-judge, agent-as-a-judge, or code evaluators.
- Turn a Signal issue into an evaluator that continuously scores new traces for that failure.
- Annotate outputs and calibrate automated scores against human judgment.

### Prove every change before you ship
- Curate datasets of test cases that capture how your agent should behave.
- Run prompt, model, or retrieval changes as experiments and compare versions side by side.
- Run datasets against your deployed agent with remote agent experiments to measure real impact.

### Use AI across the workflow
- Work with Alyx in the product to build evaluators and investigate traces.
- Instrument and operate Arize AX from Bluebox,Claude, Cursor, or Codex with the Arize AX CLI, skills, and MCP servers.

name: Claude Code Agent monitoring
description: Monitor your Claude Code coding agents with OTel.
details:
## Overview

Claude Code Monitoring provides end-to-end visibility into **Claude Code CLI usage** using its built-in **OpenTelemetry** telemetry output. The included dashboard helps engineering and AI leaders understand:

- **Spend and token consumption** over time
- **Session volume and active time**
- **API request health** (errors, latency, volume)
- **Tool activity** (tool calls, permission decisions, success rate, duration)
- **Engineering output indicators** (commits, PRs, lines added/removed)

#### What you’ll see (dashboard tiles & why it matters)

##### The dashboard summarizes 
**Total Users, Total Cost (USD), Total Tokens, Total Sessions, and Active Time** to quantify adoption and spend.  
It shows **cost over time** and **token usage over time** to spot spikes and trends.  
It breaks down **event volume by type** (`api_request`, `api_error`, `tool_decision`, `tool_result`, `user_prompt`) to understand where activity and failures occur.  

##### Engineering output signals include 
- **Lines of Code Added/Removed**, **Total Commits**, **Total PRs**, plus **LoC over time** and **PRs over time** to correlate usage with delivery.  

##### API analytics cover 
- **Cost by model**, **token & cost by model**, and **API latency over time (avg duration)** to pinpoint expensive or slow model usage.  

##### Tooling insights include:
-  **Most used tools** (e.g., bash/read/edit/write), **avg tool duration**, **permission decisions (allow/deny)**, and **tool success rate (success/failure)** to validate safety and reliability.  

##### User activity include:
-  **Avg session time**, **avg cost per session**, **avg tokens per request**, and **sessions by user** for adoption and accountability.  

##### A **recent event stream** 
- Supports debugging and drilldown of prompts, tool calls and session information

## Get started

1. Enable telemetry: `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1`.
2. Configure OTLP export to your Dynatrace OTLP endpoint (direct or via an OpenTelemetry Collector). Use delta temporality for metrics.
3. Apply the GenAI enrichment from the example: the provided OpenPipeline configuration for direct ingest, or the provided OpenTelemetry Collector configuration.
4. Run Claude Code. Telemetry is emitted automatically (no code changes).
5. Open the AI Observability app to explore Claude Code models, token usage, and traces. Optionally import the example dashboard to review cost, sessions, tool activity, and engineering output.

For setup steps, enrichment, and the dashboard, [follow the Claude Code example](https://github.com/dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-ai-agent-instrumentation-examples/tree/main/ai-coding-agents/claude-code) on GitHub.

## Details

Requirements
- Claude Code CLI with built-in OpenTelemetry telemetry support
- Dynatrace environment with OTLP ingest available
- Network access from developer machine/runner to Dynatrace OTLP endpoint (direct or via collector)

## Use cases

How teams use these insights
- **FinOps & governance:** track spend/tokens by model, detect runaway sessions, and define guardrails (budgets, thresholds, adoption controls).  
- **Reliability & performance:** monitor latency, request volume, and errors to catch degradation during peaks or provider incidents.  
- **Tool effectiveness & safety:** verify tool success, duration, and permission decisions to ensure guardrails work as intended.  
- **Adoption & productivity:** measure usage and correlate it with PRs/commits/LoC changes to evaluate AI transformation impact.

Copilot emits traces, metrics, and events using the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, covering agent invocations, LLM calls, tool and hook execution, token usage, latency, and errors. No code instrumentation is required: you configure telemetry and use Copilot normally.

Two setups are covered. Applications built on the GitHub Copilot SDK pass a telemetry configuration to the client and export through an OpenTelemetry Collector, which handles Dynatrace authentication and maps token metrics for the AI Observability app. VS Code Copilot Chat exports directly to Dynatrace using standard OTLP environment variables or enterprise-managed settings. In both cases, Copilot activity appears in the AI Observability app with models, token usage, agents, and traces.

## Get started

Choose the example that matches how you use Copilot:

- **Copilot SDK applications:** [Follow the GitHub Copilot SDK example](https://github.com/dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-ai-agent-instrumentation-examples/tree/main/ai-coding-agents/github-copilot-sdk) to run the included OpenTelemetry Collector and enable the SDK's built-in telemetry.
- **VS Code Copilot Chat:** [Follow the VS Code Copilot Chat example](https://github.com/dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-ai-agent-instrumentation-examples/tree/main/ai-coding-agents/vscode-copilot) to export telemetry directly from VS Code to Dynatrace.

## Details

### Requirements

- A Dynatrace API token with the `openTelemetryTrace.ingest` and `metrics.ingest` scopes, plus `logs.ingest` for VS Code Copilot Chat events.
- Delta temporality for metrics, which Dynatrace requires.

### Privacy

Prompt, response, tool-argument, and tool-result content is not exported by default. Enable content capture only after privacy and security approval, as it can include source code and other sensitive data.

### Cost

Copilot does not emit a native monetary cost attribute.

## Use cases

### Understand LLM behavior
See each LLM call Copilot makes, including requested and response models, token usage, finish reasons, and latency.

### Monitor tool execution
Track tool and hook calls, how long they take, and how they contribute to each agent invocation.

### Analyze agent sessions
Follow agent invocations, turns, and conversations to understand how Copilot handles requests across the CLI, VS Code, and SDK applications.

### Troubleshoot performance issues
Use traces and metrics in Dynatrace to spot slow models, token-heavy prompts, and errors.

### Explore Copilot in AI Observability
View Copilot as an AI app in the AI Observability app, with models, agents, token usage, and traces available out of the box.

## Overview

The [GenAI semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) extend OpenTelemetry with a consistent, provider-agnostic schema for AI-specific signals — model names, token counts, latency, cost, agent runs, tool calls, and evaluation results — across every major LLM provider.

This is the lowest-overhead path to AI observability: instrument once with the open standard, export over OTLP, and get full model performance, cost, and agentic workflow visibility out of the box.

## Get started

Instrumenting your AI application with native OpenTelemetry requires no additional library beyond the standard OTel SDK. Initialize a `TracerProvider`, add `gen_ai.*` attributes to your spans, and point the OTLP exporter at your Dynatrace environment. For metrics, add a `MeterProvider` and emit `gen_ai.client.token.usage` and `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` histograms alongside your traces.
